text:
anya: heads up — CI perf alert on canary for the quant-mini-batcher change landed in PR #4012. p95 latency up ~30% on small-batch INT8 workloads. canary rollout paused by deploy-bot :warning:

mike: which workload/profile? small seq length or long chat tails?

anya: repro used the bench harness with seq=32 and batch=1 (chat latency). problem shows when KV cache is cold. p50 stable, p95/p99 regress. attached profiler snippet below.

anya: ```
perf-summary: before PR #4010 (master): p95=72ms p99=120ms
perf-summary: after PR #4012 (canary): p95=94ms p99=165ms
flame: dequant_kernel + kernel_select_hotpath increased time by ~45%
KV cache hit-rate: 12% (cold skew)
```

jordan: thanks. that flame looks like dequant is being executed more often — maybe kernel selector switched to a path that emits dequant earlier for micro-batches. did someone change selection heuristics?

lina: I have a local bisect going now. initial suspicion: the packer->kernel binding change in commit 9f4d7a introduced an extra dequant call for fused-kv flow. bisecting between 9f4d7a and 3b2c0e.

ci-bot: [perf-alert] job=canary-quant-mini-batcher pipeline failed perf-thresholds (p95 > 1.2x baseline) — artifacts: https://ci.internal/perf/2356789012

mike: can you share the minimal repro command? I want to run with nvprof and the runtime counters.

lina: repro: `./bench_cli --model t5-small-quant --seq 32 --batch 1 --kv-cache=false --iters 200`

sam: I ran that with `KV cache=true` and the regression mostly goes away. seems like the extra dequant is in the path we take when cache misses trigger unpack->dequant early.

jordan: OK that narrows it. if it's cache-miss path we can either adjust the kernel selector to prefer the original fused path for cold-KV or add a cheap gate to avoid redundant dequant calls for micro-batches.

anya: lina, how's bisect progress?

lina: bisect found the offending commit: 9f4d7a. it changed `kernel_score()` to prefer lower-memory AOT kernels for short seqs; side-effect was switching to a non-fused dequant kernel.

mike: brutal. so perf win for one workload caused regression for chat. we should revert that selection change and instead add an explicit preference table keyed by (batch_size, kv_cache_state).

lina: opened PR #4015 to revert kernel preference and add a configurable selector map. small unit tests included.

deploy-bot: rollout on canary suspended (manually) due to perf-alerts. awaiting review on PR #4015.

jordan: can we also add a telemetry flag that logs kernel decisions and KV cache state so we can correlate in the future? short-term logs would avoid guessing.

anya: agreed. add a runtime flag `--emit-kernel-decisions` and a lightweight tag at trace-level. Lina please include in PR.

lina: will do. also adding a micro-batcher regression test to CI that runs the chat repro at seq=32 batch=1 with KV cold and asserts p95 within 10% of baseline.

sam: thanks — once PR #4015 lands and canary is unpaused we'll re-run the canary perf harness and check p95. I can coordinate a quick manual canary if needed.

mike: FYI we should also review our quantization rollout docs — this class of tradeoff (memory-preferring kernels vs fused-dequant for latency) should be explicit. adding to eng-runtime playbook.

anya: good call. tagging @mike for doc edit. I'll follow up with a postmortem if PR reverts the regression.

ci-bot: [artifact] perf traces uploaded: https://ci.internal/artifacts/2356789012/traces.tar.gz

lina: PR #4015 created: https://git.internal/r/4015 — includes revert + selector map + `--emit-kernel-decisions`. running CI now.

jordan: awesome. once CI passes canary can be unpaused and we should watch p50/p95 for a full smoke cycle.

anya: thanks everyone. ongoing updates here, will call for a revert/rollout once CI green. :thumbsup:
